av_event.line_text: Leanne: Ooh, that sounds amazing. I go to me mum's for Sunday dinner. She does the Yorkshire puddings and she still won't let me make them. I'm forty-one! She says I open the oven too much.
av_event.what: A man in his fifties in a work polo shirt walks into frame behind Marisol, opens the fridge door, takes out a bottle of water, closes it and walks back out of shot. Marisol does not turn round and keeps looking at the screen.

text:
B: Hello! Leanne? Hi!
A: Hiya! Oh, hello! I said in my notes I wanted to chat to you, so this is lovely.
B: Ay, me too! I'm Marisol, Leyton, East London.
A: Leanne, Castleford, West Yorkshire. Ooh, is that one of them coffee pots on your hob?
B: Yes, the moka pot! I'm Colombian, coffee is very serious for me. My last call, the man drinks instant from a broken machine. I nearly cried for him.
A: Oh no, poor lad! I'm a tea person, sorry. Builder's, bag left in.
B: Okay, I forgive you. So what do you do?
A: I'm on a packing line at a food factory, part-time. I run a flow-wrap machine and I train all the new starters and the agency lot. I love that bit, honestly, you get some right characters.
B: That's like me! I manage a shop in Walthamstow, and the new ones, I train them myself. And there's always one lovely lad who is late every single day.
A: Every place has one! Ours turns up with a Greggs and says the bus were late. The bus is never late, love, you are.
B: Ha! Exactly, exactly. And what do you do for fun?
A: Choir, I sing alto, and Zumba twice a week at the leisure centre. Six years now, I'm one of the ones at the front.
B: No! I do Zumba! Saturday mornings. But honestly I go for the chat after. And my teacher plays the same five songs every week, every week, I can do it with my eyes shut.
A: Oh, we've got a new instructor and I'm not sure about her yet. She does all these new routines and I'm stood there going, where's my Shakira gone, you know?
B: Bueno, at least she is trying! Mine, it's the same Shakira since 2015.
A: Honestly I'd swap you. Do you do anything weekends, other than Zumba?
B: Sundays I cook, big Colombian lunch, my sister comes, friends, my husband's friends. Sancocho, arepas. Sometimes twelve people in this little kitchen.
A: Ooh, that sounds amazing. I go to me mum's for Sunday dinner. She does the Yorkshire puddings and she still won't let me make them. I'm forty-one! She says I open the oven too much.
B: Ha, mothers. My mum is the same with arepas, on the phone from Colombia she tells me I make them too thin.
A: Is she still over there?
B: Yes, in Pereira. She's getting older now, eighty next year. I go back every December if I can. It's hard, you know, being far. I try not to think about it too much.
A: Aw, I bet. Me mum lives on her own, fifteen minutes away, and even that I worry. I do her shopping, her appointments. I don't know how you'd do it with an ocean in between.
B: WhatsApp, three times a week, and my sister she is very good. And I pray she don't fall, you know? That's it.
A: Yeah. Same. I say a little prayer for mine. Oh, I'm getting a bit emotional now, sorry.
B: No, no, it's normal, it's our mums! Okay, happy things. Your cat, I saw a tail!
A: Mavis! She's ancient. She were sick on the rug again this morning, right before my shift.
B: Ay, poor Mavis. And poor you.
A: Poor rug, mostly. Have you got any pets?
B: No, my husband says one day, but we have an exercise bike instead, which nobody uses.
A: Ha! Same as my rowing machine. It's a coat stand now. Right, are you watching Strictly, because
